paper_sections.title: Binge Eating (BE) and Obesity: Brain Activity and Psychological Measures before and after Roux-En-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB)
3.4.3. Change in Activation from Baseline to 4 Months Post (T1 > T2)

description.value: The study examined brain responses to food and non-food visual cues, binge-eating status, psychological measures, and changes approximately four months after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass compared with a non-treatment control group.

design.value: Prospective longitudinal study of healthy women with class III obesity, including 15 women who underwent RYGB and 13 BMI-matched women who did not undergo treatment. Participants completed fMRI approximately 1 month before and 4 months after bariatric surgery, with the NT group assessed at a matched interval. Analyses compared treatment groups and binge-eating status at baseline, at 4 months, and for baseline-to-post-treatment changes.

name.value: Questionnaire of Eating and Weight Patterns Revised (QEWP-R)

description.value: Questionnaire used to assess binge-eating status at baseline and again at 4 months.
Questionnaire used at baseline in conjunction with the QEWP-R for binge-eating assessment.
Participants were assessed according to the DSM-5 and classified as BE when they endorsed overeating with loss of control and met full or subthreshold criteria.

The EMAQ assesses emotional eating in response to both positive and negative emotions and situations. It contains 22 questions, with mean scores calculated for positive emotions and situations and negative emotions and situations.

The PFS assesses the impact of current food-abundant environments, including appetite-related thoughts, feelings, and motivations, at three levels of food proximity: food available (Abstract), food present (Presence), and food tasted (Pleasure).
Questionnaire used to reassess binge-eating status at 4 months; it included modified questions pertaining to bariatric surgery in place of the EDE-Q.
A Tanita scale employing bioelectrical impedance analysis was used to measure body fat.

task_description.value: Visual stimuli were presented to participants in the scanner via goggles in six runs. Each run was made up of 10 stimuli of the same type (HEF, LEF, or NF), and each type was repeated twice with different stimuli. Ten stimuli were presented for four seconds each, with a 52-second pre-stimulus baseline and a 40-second post-stimulus baseline.

stimuli.value: HEF stimuli included cakes, ice cream, and fast foods. LEF stimuli consisted of fruits and vegetables. NF stimuli consisted of basic office supplies, such as tape, staplers, and rubber bands. All HEF stimuli had an energy density of at least 3.5 kcal/g, and all LEF stimuli had an energy density less than 1 kcal/g.

instrument.value: 1.5 GE Tesla twin-speed scanner with supine quadrature RF head coil

description.value: Functional T2*-weighted images were obtained with a gradient echo pulse sequence. Three-plane localization was used to verify head position. Six runs were collected. Each run contained 36 whole-brain scans consisting of 25 contiguous slices parallel to the AC/PC line.

model_settings.value: First-level regressors were created by convolving the onset of each condition with the canonical HRF with duration of 40 s. Contrasts were created for Food > NF and HEF > LEF at T1, T2, and T1 > T2.

model_type.value: second-level multiple regression and group random effects model

model_settings.value: Contrasts of parameter estimates from the first-level models were passed to second-level multiple regression analyses with predictor variables for experimental group (BE vs. NB; RYGB vs. NT) and BMI as a nuisance covariate. Main comparisons included overall effects at T1, T2, and T1 > T2 and two-way interactions between experimental and intervention groups.

Given outliers, non-normal data, and unequal variances, 1,000 bootstrap samples were performed using a bias corrected and accelerated confidence interval. Test statistics for the original, unsampled data were reported.

estimator.value: 1,000 nonparametric bootstrap samples with a bias corrected and accelerated confidence interval
